Antwoord op vragen van het lid Karabulut over derubricering bilaterale verdragen van Nederland en de VS over plaatsing van kernwapens in Nederland

An MP asked why the government did not itself release nineteen documents on US nuclear weapons in the Netherlands, whether further declassification is planned, and why MoUs on nuclear weapons remain secret. The ministers answered that security and alliance obligations prevent disclosure of locations, numbers and bilateral arrangements, while some older treaties were declassified where NATO agreed.
On grounds of state security, no statements can be made about secret treaties between the Netherlands and other countries.
Op grond van overwegingen van staatsveiligheid kunnen geen mededelingen worden gedaan over geheime verdragen tussen Nederland en andere landen.
Antwoord op vragen van het lid Van Helvert over de berichtgeving van de Veteranenombudsman over de behandelingsduur van de schadevergoeding voor invalide veteranen

An MP from the CDA asked the Minister of Defence about the Veterans Ombudsman's findings that compensation for disabled veterans is handled too slowly, and about proposed fixes such as digitising medical files, a single medical assessment and a care coordinator. The minister acknowledged the delays, said Defence aims to settle claims within two years, is positive about the proposals and is working on a reform of the benefits system, though she declined to commit to a firm date for digitisation.
Defence aims, together with the parties involved, to settle the compensation within two years.
Defensie streeft er naar – samen met betrokken partijen – de schadevergoeding binnen twee jaar af te handelen.
Antwoord op vragen van het lid Van den Bosch over het bericht waarin oud-Dutchbatters vinden dat er alsnog erkenning moet komen van overheid, defensie en media

An MP from the VVD asked the Minister of Defence about reports that former Dutchbat veterans want formal recognition and adequate care, and how many need professional help that they are not receiving. The Minister says the Borstlap report and recommendations will be acted upon in a policy response, funded in spring budget decisions, and that all Dutchbat-III veterans will be invited to contact the care desk.
All Dutchbat-III veterans and their families will shortly receive a letter explicitly inviting them to contact the care desk if they still need professional help due to the deployment.

Alle Dutchbat-III-veteranen en hun thuisfront ontvangen binnenkort een brief, waarin zij expliciet worden uitgenodigd om contact op te nemen met het zorgloket indien zij nog professionele hulp behoeven vanwege de uitzending.
Antwoord op vragen van het lid Wassenberg over het uitbreiden van een Natura 2000-gebied met een voormalig defensieterrein

Wassenberg (PvdD) asks whether the former Defence terrain near Meijendel Natura 2000 area, which The Hague council wants returned to nature, will be added to the protected area, and whether Zuid-Holland can help acquire it. The minister answers that the Rijksvastgoedbedrijf is examining with the municipality, province and stakeholders whether transfer is possible, aiming for clarity by September 2021, while the province plays a facilitating role.
The aim is to have clarity on this by September 2021.
Het streven is hier in september 2021 duidelijkheid over te hebben.
Antwoord op vragen van het lid Karabulut over het verzoek voor inzet van het Defensiepersoneel ter ondersteuning van het zorgpersoneel

An SP MP asks the Defence Minister how many requests for military support to healthcare staff were received, which were granted or refused, how priorities against foreign missions are set, whether more personnel can be freed, and how a motion on this was implemented. The minister answers that 25 requests since October 2020 were granted, that priority is balanced against foreign missions and core tasks, that up to 160 (later 100) medical staff support UMC Utrecht, and that 1,000 personnel are on standby, without naming refused requests.
Defence must ensure that ongoing missions abroad are carried out and properly prepared.
Defensie moet zekerstellen dat de lopende missies in het buitenland worden uitgevoerd en terdege worden voorbereid
Antwoord op vragen van het lid Karabulut over burgerdoden in Uruzgan

MP Karabulut asked the ministers of Defence and Foreign Affairs about a reported 2007 incident in the Chora valley in Uruzgan where a Dutch veteran said civilians may have been killed, including questions on reports, rules of engagement, a complaints channel and civilian casualty counts. The Minister of Defence said the archives had not yet matched the described incident, a veteran interview had been held, a new archive search and consultation with the Public Prosecution Service were under way, and that a fact-finding inquiry by the OM had been started.
On the basis of this, I will, after consultation with the Public Prosecution Service, decide whether or not to launch an investigation.
Op basis hiervan zal ik, na overleg met het OM, besluiten al dan niet een onderzoek in te stellen.
Antwoord op vragen van het lid Van den Bosch over hulpprojecten in Hawija uit de Defensiebegroting

An MP asked the Defence Minister whether the 4 million euro for recovery in Hawija after an airstrike, reportedly drawn from the Defence budget, was known to her, whether the promised information on the project had been given, and how the funding was sourced and at whose expense. The minister confirmed awareness and promised the earlier commitment, and said the money comes from the International Security Budget within Defence without cutting other Defence spending.
To fund the voluntary compensation for the Hawija community, the International Security Budget (BIV), which forms part of the Defence budget, is used.
Voor de financiering van de vrijwillige vergoeding voor de gemeenschap in Hawija wordt gebruik gemaakt van het Budget Internationale Veiligheid (BIV) dat onderdeel vormt van de Defensiebegroting.
Antwoord op vragen van het lid Van den Nieuwenhuijzen over de beveiliging van ICT bij het Ministerie van Defensie

An MP from GroenLinks asked the Minister of Defence whether a journalist left alone in a waiting room with network access points, and whether other visitors could likewise access the Defence network, and how sensitive information and ICT security are managed. The minister answered that the waiting room offers only a guest internet connection, that visitors are escorted and technical measures block network access, and that Defence runs regular security assessments, including with the intelligence services.
Targeted attempts by visitors to obtain information on site are not known.
Doelgerichte pogingen door bezoekers om op locatie informatie buit te maken zijn niet bekend.
Antwoord op vragen van het lid Verhoeven inzake delen inloggegevens vergadering EU defensieministers

An MP asked the Defence Minister for the metadata of two photos showing a video-conference login link of an EU defence ministers' meeting, which leaked access to the meeting. The minister answered that she took the photos at home on 20 November 2020 at 09:23 and 09:37 and gave the timestamps, but did not address the broader issue of how the link was exposed.
This photo, as I also stated during question hour on 24 November, was taken by me personally at 09:23.
Deze foto is, zoals ik ook in het vragenuurtje van 24 november jl. aangaf, door mijzelf gemaakt, om 09:23 uur.
Antwoord op vragen van de leden Belhaj en Sjoerdsma over het bericht dat Australische militairen 39 burgers en gevangenen executeerden in Afghanistan

Two D66 MPs asked whether the ministers knew of reports that Australian soldiers executed 39 civilians and prisoners in Afghanistan, what the Dutch government knew and when, whether Dutch soldiers worked closely with Australian forces, and whether any war crimes investigation was conducted. The minister answered that the Australian inquiry shared no information beforehand, that Dutch soldiers were interviewed only in confidential interviews in 2018, that Dutch-Australian cooperation existed within Task Force Uruzgan, and that the Netherlands conducted no investigation into possible Australian war crimes.
The record of these confidential interviews was not made available to the cabinet or to the interviewed soldiers by the Australian inquiry commission.
Het verslag van deze vertrouwelijke interviews is niet door de Australische onderzoekscommissie aan het kabinet of aan de geïnterviewde militairen ter beschikking gesteld.
Antwoord op vragen van het lid Karabulut over de Australische excessen in Afghanistan en de reactie hierop

An SP MP asked the Defence and Foreign Affairs ministers about Australian special forces killing 39 civilians and detainees in Afghanistan, including in Uruzgan where the Netherlands was active, and how the Netherlands responded. The Defence Minister answered that no Dutch involvement has been found so far, that Defence is conducting an internal inventory of joint operations and Australian recommendations, and described the Dutch-Australian coordination and separate command lines in 2006-2010.
If there is cause to do so, the cabinet will inform the House as soon as possible of the findings of the inventory.
Indien hier aanleiding toe is, stelt het kabinet de Kamer zo snel mogelijk op de hoogte van de bevindingen van de inventarisatie.
Antwoord op vragen van de leden Karabulut, Ploumen en Van Ojik over het Nederlandse kernwapenbeleid

Three MPs asked the foreign and defence ministers about NATO's decision to publicise the nuclear dimension of exercise Steadfast Noon, transparency on Dutch nuclear policy, the Secretary-General's visit to Volkel, and whether nuclear sharing breaches the Non-Proliferation Treaty. The ministers answered that transparency is being increased within alliance limits, that exercise details and US nuclear locations remain classified, and that nuclear sharing arrangements predate and are consistent with the NPT.
As your House is aware, no statements can be made on the numbers and locations of American nuclear weapons present in Europe, due to alliance and legally binding agreements.

Zoals uw Kamer bekend, kunnen over aantallen en locaties van in Europa aanwezige Amerikaanse kernwapens op grond van bondgenootschappelijke en juridisch bindende afspraken geen mededelingen worden gedaan.
Antwoord op vragen van het lid Karabulut over transparantie met betrekking tot het oefenen van het gebruik van atoomwapens

An SP MP asked the Minister of Defence about transparency on nuclear-weapons exercises and transport at Volkel air base, and about the government's transparency policy, including whether earlier answers needed correcting. The minister answered that Netherlands pursues transparency within NATO agreements, confirmed a NATO exercise with a nuclear dimension was disclosed this year while details stay classified, and declined to give locations or numbers of US nuclear weapons, citing security and binding agreements.
Regarding the numbers and locations of American nuclear weapons present in Europe, no statements can likewise be made, on the basis of alliance and legally binding agreements.
Over aantallen en locaties van in Europa aanwezige Amerikaanse kernwapens kunnen, op grond van bondgenootschappelijke en juridisch bindende afspraken, eveneens geen mededelingen worden gedaan.

Antwoord op vragen van de leden De Roon, Fritsma en Markuszower over de beroerde informatievoorziening aan de Tweede Kamer inzake de inspectie van een koopvaardijschip door marineschip de Zr. Ms. De Ruyter

PVV MPs asked the Justice, Defence and Foreign Affairs ministers why information on the Dutch navy's boarding of a merchant ship (Zr. Ms. De Ruyter) was withheld, and asked about the legal basis, the cargo, sanctions and links to Operation Irini. Minister Grapperhaus refused details citing an ongoing criminal investigation, cited the Criminal Code as legal basis, denied any link to Irini, and promised to inform parliament once possible.
As is customary, your House will be informed as soon as the still ongoing criminal investigation allows for this.
Zoals te doen gebruikelijk zal uw Kamer worden geïnformeerd zodra daar gezien het thans nog lopende strafrechtelijk onderzoek de mogelijkheid toe bestaat.
Antwoord op vragen van de leden Schonis, Belhaj en De Groot over munitiedumps in de Deltawateren en Noordzeekust

Three D66 MPs asked the government about the munitions dump in the Oosterschelde and North Sea sites, including the risks, monitoring, clean-up or capping costs, and whether a dedicated management fund exists. The government answered that research results will be sent to parliament in 2021, that monitoring shows no danger, that no clean-up or capping is planned under current assessments, and that only existing monitoring budgets are available.
The results will then be submitted to your House in 2021.
De resultaten worden dan in 2021 aan uw Kamer aangeboden.
Antwoord op vragen van het lid Belhaj over het bericht dat Defensie gedragsbeïnvloedingsmethodes ontwikkelt voor moderne oorlogsvoering

An MP asks the Minister of Defence about reports that the Dutch armed forces develop behavioural influence methods (BDM) for modern warfare, including whether an ethical framework is needed, the risk of pulling civilians into conflict, comparisons with other countries, training, the purchase from a firm linked to Cambridge Analytica, and whether a public debate is needed. The Minister answers that existing legal and ethical frameworks apply, that civilians are not drawn into conflict unlawfully, that a debate is welcome, and that the method is currently not used abroad.
Yes. Since 2014 it has been government policy that departments, including Defence, invest in building behavioural science expertise to improve government policy.
Ja. Sinds 2014 is het kabinetsbeleid dat de departementen, waaronder Defensie investeren in het opbouwen van gedragswetenschappelijke expertise om het overheidsbeleid te verbeteren.
Antwoord op vragen van de leden Van Dam en Van Helvert over de verkoop van Nederlandse MP5’s in een Maltese wapenhandel

MPs Van Dam and Van Helvert asked about Dutch MP5 submachine guns reportedly sold by a Maltese arms dealer, whether the sale involved a batch of 850 ministry weapons, what rules apply to resale, and oversight of onward sales. The state secretary answered that no weapons were sold to that firm, that 850 surplus MP5s went to the Dutch defence supplier TBM, and that Defence has no sight of further resale by the manufacturer or its partners.
Defence does not keep track of further (onward) sales by the manufacturer or an authorised trading partner of the manufacturer.
Defensie houdt geen zicht op de verdere (door-)verkoop door de fabrikant of erkende (handels)partner van de fabrikant.
Antwoord op vragen van de leden De Roon, Popken en Markuszower over een inspectie door het marineschip Zr. Ms. De Ruyter

MPs De Roon, Popken and Markuszower asked whether the frigate De Ruyter carried out a ship inspection over a possible sanctions violation, which vessel and flag were involved, what evidence existed, and with whom findings were shared. The government confirmed the inspection, said details could not be disclosed because a criminal investigation by the Public Prosecution Service is ongoing and shared findings only with that service, and declined to give operational details of the ship's operations.
As you know, as Minister of Justice and Security I do not make substantive statements about an ongoing criminal investigation.
Zoals bij u bekend doe ik als Minister van Justitie en Veiligheid geen inhoudelijke mededelingen over een lopend strafrechtelijk onderzoek.
Antwoord op vragen van de leden Van den Nieuwenhuijzen, Karabulut en Kerstens over het artikel 'Een soft maar gevaarlijk wapen: moderne oorlogsvoering richt zich op beïnvloeding van de bevolking'

MPs from GroenLinks, SP and PvdA asked the Defence Minister about the use of the Behavioural Dynamics Methodology (BDM) by the armed forces, its origins linked to Cambridge Analytica's parent company, the absence of an ethical framework, legal review, a Caribbean pilot, procurement, MIVD overlap, oversight and parliamentary information. The Minister answered that BDM is a legitimate tool operated within existing legal and ethical frameworks, that parliament was not separately informed of the SCL-Defence purchase, that a procurement process started in 2019, and that PsyOps are approved by the political-strategic level with parliament informed under existing procedures.
Defence bought the BDM course in 2017 not from Cambridge Analytica but from SCL-Defence.
Defensie kocht de BDM-cursus in 2017 niet bij Cambridge Analytica, maar bij SCL-Defence.
Antwoord op vragen van het lid Voordewind over het bericht dat Turkije het S400-luchtafweersysteem getest heeft op F-35- en F22-toestellen

The ChristenUnie MP Voordewind asked the Ministers of Defence and Foreign Affairs whether reports that Turkey tested its S-400 air defence system against F-35 and F-22 aircraft are accurate, how the government views this, and whether it will raise the matter at NATO. The Minister could not confirm the report, stated serious concerns about Turkey's S-400 acquisition raised bilaterally and in NATO, declined to share operational details of the F-35 for security reasons, and saw no reason to raise the issue at the October NATO defence ministers' meeting for now.
Regarding the specific operational capabilities of the F-35, including claims about possible vulnerabilities of the system, I cannot provide your House with further information for security reasons.

Over de specifieke operationele capaciteiten van de F-35 inclusief beweringen over eventuele kwetsbaarheden van het systeem kan ik uw Kamer vanuit veiligheidsoverwegingen geen verdere informatie doen toekomen.
Antwoord op vragen van het lid Bosman over financiering onder het Europees Defensiefonds

An MP asked the Defence Minister whether co-financing for European Defence Fund projects could come from member states and how much Dutch co-financing would be needed, including whether Economic Affairs could contribute. The minister answered that the co-financing rule does not specify who pays, that no specific budget line exists yet, that options are being mapped in an interdepartmental group, and that Dutch firms received limited EDF funding.
The amount of the co-financing and the distribution within the consortia are commercially confidential.
De hoogte van de cofinanciering en de verdeling binnen de consortia zijn commercieel vertrouwelijk.
Antwoord op vragen van het lid Karabulut over een zoekgeraakte wapenleverantie in Libië in 2017

An SP MP asked the Foreign and Defence Ministers to give a full account of the 2017 disappearance of weapons and communications equipment shipped to Tripoli to protect the Dutch embassy, and why Parliament was not informed. The minister responded with a timeline of the shipment and loss, confidentially briefed Parliament earlier, but withheld the types and quantities of goods on security grounds and gave no further details.
We do not disclose the nature of the goods for security reasons.
Over de aard van de goederen doen we uit veiligheidsoverwegingen geen mededelingen.
Antwoord op vragen van de leden Belhaj en Sjoerdsma over het bericht ‘Rusland betaalde Afghaanse strijders om Amerikaanse militairen te doden’

MPs Belhaj and Sjoerdsma asked whether the government confirmed reports that Russia paid Afghan fighters to kill US soldiers, whether US intelligence had informed the Netherlands, and whether Dutch troops in Afghanistan were at higher risk. The ministers answered that the government does not publicly comment on cooperation with foreign intelligence services or specific intelligence, that allied services would normally share information affecting each other's soldiers, and that general threat levels are monitored with precautions taken where needed.
As is well known, the cabinet makes no public statements about cooperation with and between foreign intelligence services.
Het kabinet doet, zoals bekend, in het openbaar geen mededelingen over de samenwerking met en tussen buitenlandse inlichtingendiensten.
Antwoord op vragen van het lid Gijs Van Dijk en Kerstens over een vlucht van twee Apache gevechtshelikopters boven Texel

MPs Van Dijk and Kerstens asked the Defence Minister about Apache helicopters flying low over Texel on 17 June 2020 for the TV programme Hunted, including noise and nesting-bird disturbance, and whether the mayor was informed in time. The minister said the flights respected legal minimum altitudes, that Defence joined the filming to recruit and train, and that the mayor should have been involved earlier, but denied the event fell under the emergency ordinance.
These evaluation talks show that, given the specific environment, the training and the filming, it would have been better to involve and inform the municipality and the mayor earlier.
Uit deze evaluatiegesprekken blijkt dat vanwege de specifieke omgeving, de training én opnames het beter was geweest om de gemeente en de burgemeester eerder te betrekken en te informeren.
Antwoord op vragen van het lid Karabulut over het debat over burgerslachtoffers in Irak op 14 mei 2020

The SP MP Karabulut asked the Defence Minister about civilian casualties from the 2015 Dutch airstrike on Hawija, including death tolls, CENTCOM verification, the ICRC list, allied refusals, transparency rules and compensation. The Minister largely referred back to earlier letters, declined to answer several questions on CENTCOM's counting system as outside her ministry's control, and pointed to forthcoming proposals on informing parliament about civilian harm and on compensation.
Antwoord op vragen van het lid Belhaj over het bericht ‘Dure borrels, feestjes en uitjes: Defensie legt miljoenenuitgaven aan banden’

An MP asked the Defence Minister about reports of costly staff parties and asked for an explanation of the Walibi family day cost breakdown, the pressures behind it, and new spending rules. The minister gave the per-FTE cost figures, a breakdown of the roughly 630,000 euro Walibi event, extra KMar funding, gift rules and new limits on team events, without any explicit commitment to further action.
See below the breakdown of the costs for the staff outing.
Zie onderstaand de verdeling van de kosten voor het personeelsuitje

Antwoord op vragen van de leden Van Dam en Van Helvert over het rapport van de Algemene Rekenkamer 'Digitalisering aan de grens; Cybersecurity van het grenstoezicht door de Koninklijke Marechaussee op Schiphol'

Two CDA MPs asked the Justice and Defence ministers about the Court of Audit report on cybersecurity of border control systems at Schiphol run by the Royal Marechaussee, including data ownership, transfer of the self-service system to Schiphol N.V., security approval, testing frequency and monitoring. The government answered in detail, acknowledging delays in approval and resource limits, while withholding some test results as classified and promising further measures on protecting vital infrastructure.
The research results of the counter system are classified and therefore cannot be shared.
De onderzoeksresultaten van het baliesysteem zijn gerubriceerd en kunnen daarom niet gedeeld worden.
Antwoord op vragen van het lid Van Raan over een nieuw onderzoek naar de risico’s op botsingen met vogels als gevolg van de opening van Lelystad Airport

An MP asks the government whether a new bird-radar study showing higher-altitude and night-time bird movements undermines the bird-strike risk assessment in the updated environmental impact report for Lelystad Airport, and whether the report should be re-tested or redone. The minister answers that the new method does not change the conclusions, that the same radar data was used, that the risk assessment remains valid, and that no guarantee against bird strikes can be given, but declines to commit to a new or independent review.
No. The relevant scientific article by Kranstauber and others does not concern Lelystad Airport.
Nee. Het betreffende wetenschappelijke artikel van Kranstauber en anderen gaat niet over Lelystad Airport.
Antwoord op de vraag van het lid Van Raak over het niet naar behoren beantwoorden van Kamervragen

An MP asked the Defence Minister, on behalf of the Interior Minister, whether the government invokes state interest per question when declining to answer his questions about Dutch involvement in the Rubicon espionage operation and the Maximator eavesdropping network, and for each refusal to give reasons, risks and expected harm. The government replied that no state-interest exemption under article 68 of the Constitution was invoked because no information was refused, that intelligence matters are handled confidentially via the CIVD, and it referred to the 'open unless' principle.
There is no invocation of the state interest under article 68 of the Constitution in answering your questions, because no information is being refused.

Er is bij de beantwoording van de door u gestelde vragen geen sprake van een beroep op het belang van de staat als bedoeld in artikel 68 van de Grondwet, omdat er geen sprake is van het weigeren van verstrekking van informatie.
Antwoord op vragen van de leden Den Boer, Özütok en Van Raak over het bericht ‘Van 2 uitvaarten per week naar 2 per dag: uitvaartondernemer Marjan Damen draait overuren’

MPs asked the ministers about reports that funeral directors were overstretched by rising COVID-19 deaths, including capacity in mortuaries, the role of Defence and coordination, protective equipment, coffin supply and Islamic and Jewish burial rights. The minister answered that the sector is coping, that a coordination point and Defence support can be arranged if needed, that mortuary and coffin capacity is sufficient with contingency plans, and that burial options exist.
I indeed receive questions from the funeral sector about the Corona crisis, including about the cabinet's measures and RIVM guidelines.
Ik ontvang inderdaad vragen uit de uitvaartsector over de Corona-crisis, waaronder ook over de maatregelen van het kabinet en de richtlijnen van het RIVM.

Antwoord op vragen van het lid Karabulut over de rol van de Karel Doorman in de Caribische Zee en de oproep van voormalig VN-chef Egeland om economische sancties tegen diverse landen, waaronder Venezuela op te heffen

An SP MP asked why the Karel Doorman is deployed for maritime border patrol near the Leeward Antilles, whether it joins anti-drug operations against Venezuela, and whether the government will support lifting sanctions on Venezuela during the pandemic. The minister answered that the deployment supports the Caribbean Coast Guard against possible COVID-19-related migration, corrected a press release wrongly suggesting anti-drug patrols, and stated that sanctions should not hinder humanitarian aid while the EU keeps them targeted.
The cited Ministry of Defence news item unfortunately contained an editorial error, which gave the impression that the Karel Doorman could also be deployed for anti-drug patrols.

Het aangehaalde nieuwsbericht van het Ministerie van Defensie bevatte helaas een redactionele fout, waardoor de indruk werd gewekt dat Zr.Ms. Karel Doorman tevens kon worden ingezet voor anti-drugspatrouilles.
Antwoord op vragen van de leden Van den Bosch en Bosman over het bericht ‘Defensie laat veteranen met klachten veel te lang wachten’

MPs Van den Bosch and Bosman (VVD) asked the Defence Minister about reports that the National Ombudsman found veterans with complaints waiting too long for compensation claims, and what Defence would do about it. The minister acknowledged the complaints in general terms, said delays are partly inherent and partly due to other parties, and listed existing measures (RVS evaluation, doubled legal staff) plus detailed claim statistics, while pointing to the ombudsman's pending investigation.
I am aware that the processing time is experienced as too long.
Ik ben mij ervan bewust dat de afhandelingsduur als te lang wordt ervaren.
Antwoord op vragen van het lid Van Raak over het niet naar behoren beantwoorden van Kamervragen

MP Van Raak asked the Defence Minister why questions he posed on 14 April about the Dutch role in intelligence operations Rubicon and Maximator were treated as actual and operational matters. The Minister replied that, in line with earlier answers, the government does not comment publicly on the knowledge and methods of the intelligence services, since confirming or denying operations or cooperation could reveal those methods.

Answering questions about possible operations or cooperation arrangements amounts to confirming or denying that these operations or arrangements exist, and can thereby give insight into the methods and knowledge level of the services.

Het beantwoorden van vragen over mogelijke operaties of samenwerkingsverbanden is een bevestiging of ontkenning van het bestaan van deze operaties of samenwerkingsverbanden en kan daarmee inzicht geven in de werkwijze en het kennisniveau van de diensten.
Antwoord op vragen van het lid Baudet over het verkeerd informeren van de Kamer omtrent het bombardement in Hawija

An MP asks the Defence Minister why the House was misinformed about the 2017 Dutch air strike in Hawija, including whether US warnings of civilian deaths were withheld and why a US investigation was not shared. The minister mostly refers back to earlier letters, admits an administrative error in counting civilian casualties, and denies having misinformed the House or planning consequences.
Antwoord op vragen van de leden De Roon en Popken over de waarnemingen van De Zr. Ms. De Ruyter van het incident in de Golf van Oman

MPs De Roon and Popken asked what the Dutch frigate De Ruyter observed of the reported Iranian seizure of the chemical tanker SC Taipei, whether Iran was involved and whether Iran's provocations should be condemned. The Defence Minister declined to share observations for operational reasons, said no cargo was seized as far as the government knows, and stated the government's commitment to de-escalation through the EMASoH mission.
No statements can be made about the observations of Zr. Ms. De Ruyter for operational reasons.
Over de waarnemingen van De Zr. Ms. De Ruyter kunnen om operationele redenen geen mededelingen worden gedaan.
Antwoord op vragen van het lid Karabulut over Nederlandse militairen in Afghanistan

An SP MP asked the Defence and Foreign Affairs ministers about the withdrawal and rotation of Dutch troops in Afghanistan during the COVID-19 pandemic, including what 'essential' personnel means and whether NATO can help fight the virus there. The minister answered that non-essential staff were temporarily withdrawn, explained the quarantine and remote-advice arrangements, and said NATO is not the primary actor for COVID-19 aid in Afghanistan.
As your House was informed on 24 March (reference 2020D11584), the commander of the Resolute Support mission ordered that personnel not essential to continuing the mission be temporarily withdrawn.
(kenmerk 2020D11584 ) is door de commandant van de Resolute Support missie opdracht gegeven het personeel dat niet essentieel is voor de voortzetting van de missie, tijdelijk terug te trekken.
Antwoord op vragen van het lid Karabulut over wapenimporten uit Turkije

An MP asked whether Turkish military imports cost the Netherlands over 16 million dollars in two months, which systems were bought and whether the government would press allies to stop imports from Turkey given Syria and human rights concerns. The government could not verify the figures, said the Ministry of Defence only bought maintenance and modification services for Stinger launching systems, and refused to ask allies for an import ban, arguing that export controls are the more effective tool.
No independent figures are available on imports of military goods from Turkey in the first two months of 2020.
Er zijn geen onafhankelijke cijfers beschikbaar ten aanzien van de import van militaire goederen uit Turkije in de eerste twee maanden van 2020.
Antwoord op vragen van het lid Karabulut over het aanpassen van de oefening Defender 2020

An MP asked the Defence Minister whether she had warned the Defender 2020 exercise leadership about COVID-19 risks, why the exercise was not ended, and what legal basis and Host Nation Support provisions were used. The minister answered that the US largely cancelled the exercise, that troop movements through the Netherlands were fully cancelled, that health precautions were taken, and that the Host Nation Support request was withdrawn, but did not directly answer whether the Netherlands urged cancellation or consulted other governments.
The US has largely cancelled the Defender 2020 exercise.
De VS heeft de oefening Defender 2020 grotendeels afgelast.
Antwoord op vragen van het lid Belhaj over het bericht ‘Overheid voor rechter om etnische profileren: ‘Zo vernederend dat je kleur bepalend is’

An MP asked about reports of ethnic profiling by the Royal Netherlands Marechaussee (KMar) at Eindhoven Airport, including the use of ethnicity as a risk indicator in mobile border checks, its proportionality, complaints and evaluations. The government answered that ethnicity is never a standalone indicator and is used only with other objective indicators, that no legal changes are needed, and that complaints are handled through an independent committee while evaluations and optimisation of profiling methods continue.
Ethnicity is never a standalone risk factor, but is always applied as an indicator in combination with other indicators.
Etniciteit is nooit een op zichzelf staande risicofactor, maar wordt als indicator altijd in combinatie met andere indicatoren toegepast.
Antwoord op vragen van het lid De Roon over het gebruik van MANPADS in de Syrische provincie Idlib en de risico’s voor de burgerluchtvaart

An MP asked the ministers of Foreign Affairs, Defence and Infrastructure whether Turkey or Turkish-backed groups used MANPADS in Idlib, whether Turkey's policy was being raised, and what the risks to civil aviation were. The government said it could not confirm who operated the systems, that the matter was raised diplomatically with Turkey, and that Dutch airlines avoid Syrian airspace so no further investigation was needed.
The cabinet does not make public statements about which groups have or have not received NLA support from the Netherlands.
229 ) doet het kabinet in het openbaar geen uitspraken over de groepen die al-dan-niet NLA-steun hebben ontvangen van Nederland.
Antwoord op vragen van het lid Karabulut over de mogelijke inzet van delen van de krijgsmacht ter ondersteuning van de bestrijding van de COVID-19 pandemie

The SP MP Karabulut asked the Defence Minister whether Defence would suspend ship and unit programmes to support COVID-19 response, offer ICU places, and what role military hospitals, engineers and transport could play, plus questions on personnel limits, the Wuhan evacuees, hospital cooperation and protection of deployed troops. The Minister answered that Defence supports the crisis response on request, lists loans of planners and medical staff, 65 ventilators to hospitals and Caribbean territories, food-bank support and Caribbean border and public-order assistance, and that deployments are reviewed continuously.
When, what and in what way Defence deploys capabilities is discussed during the crisis on the basis of a request from civil authorities and in consultation with the other departments.
Wanneer, wat voor en op welke manier Defensie capaciteiten inzet, wordt gedurende de crisis op basis van een verzoek van civiele autoriteiten en in overleg met de andere departementen besproken.
Antwoord op vragen het lid Karabulut over een boek over de missie in Uruzgan, Afghanistan

MPs Karabulut asked the ministers of Foreign Affairs and Defence about a book by a veteran claiming there were no Taliban in Uruzgan and that Dutch force use was excessive and civilian casualties were high. The government rejects the portrayal, says it cannot reliably count enemy or civilian casualties, and says the international mission helped Afghanistan.
Defence did not keep a registration of the number of enemy combatants killed as a result of Dutch action.
Defensie heeft geen registratie bijgehouden over het aantal gevallen vijandelijke strijders ten gevolge van Nederlands optreden.
Antwoord op vragen van de leden Sjoerdsma, Belhaj en Groothuizen over een Nederlandse bijdrage aan een gereactiveerde ‘Sophia-missie’

MPs Sjoerdsma, Belhaj and Groothuizen asked the ministers about the Berlin Libya conference, the EU arms embargo monitoring role, reactivating the Sophia mission, humanitarian and migration effects, and a Dutch contribution. The government welcomed the Berlin outcomes, said EUNAVFOR MED Irini (succeeding Sophia) will implement the UN arms embargo, and said a Dutch contribution of staff officers in Rome is likely while further capacity decisions await military advice.
The cabinet is still considering a possible contribution with other capabilities.
Het kabinet beraadt zich nog op een eventuele bijdrage met andere capaciteiten.
Antwoord op vragen van de leden Bosman en Koopmans over het bericht  ‘U.S. can’t continue’ tolerating Russian ‘noncompliance’ on Open Skies, Esper says’

MPs Bosman and Koopmans asked whether Defence Minister Esper's concerns about Russian non-compliance with the Open Skies treaty had been shared with allies and whether the Netherlands shares them and is acting on them. Minister Blok answered that the US concerns were raised bilaterally, in NATO and the OSCE, that the Netherlands shares them, has raised them with Moscow and in the OSCC, and has pressed for compliance and the treaty's value without joining any formal joint pressure beyond NATO questionnaires.
The Netherlands, like the US, is of the view that all parties must comply with the obligations under the treaty.
Nederland is net als de VS van mening dat alle partijen zich aan de verplichtingen onder het verdrag dienen te houden.
Antwoord op vragen van het lid Karabulut over verloop Defender 2020 naar aanleiding van maatregelen in het kader van de bestrijding van Coivd-19 pandemie

An SP MP asked the Defence Minister what EUCOM's decision to reduce US participation in exercise Defender 2020 means for Dutch involvement, whether only the media day was cancelled, whether Dutch participation would be cancelled for pandemic reasons, and what the new gathering limits mean for Defence exercises. The minister replied that the planned movement of a US armoured brigade through the Netherlands will not proceed, that Defence will keep supporting allies until they leave, and referred to a letter on COVID-19 impacts on missions and exercises.
The planned movement of a US combat brigade through the Netherlands will not be continued.
De geplande troepenverplaatsing van een Amerikaanse gevechtsbrigade door Nederland wordt niet voortgezet.
Antwoord op vragen van de leden Sjoerdsma en Belhaj over de EU Battlegroup

Two MPs asked the Foreign and Defence Ministers about the EU Battlegroup: whether the Netherlands leads it with Germany in 2020, why Battlegroups have never been deployed, and whether they could support UN missions. The minister confirmed the Netherlands' contribution and explained that unanimity, operational and financial obstacles have blocked deployment, while committing to explore a Battlegroup role in a UN mission before summer 2020.
I promised the House to inform it about this before summer 2020. I will keep this commitment.
Ik beloofde de Kamer hierover voor de zomer 2020 te informeren. Ik zal deze toezegging gestand doen.
Antwoord op vragen van het lid Karabulut over offensieve inzet van Afghaanse agenten in de periode 2011-2013

An SP MP asks the Prime Minister and the ministers of Foreign Affairs and Defence whether the Chamber was misled about offensive deployment of Dutch-trained Afghan police in Kunduz (2011-2013), as a post-mission assessment suggests, and why the final evaluation did not report it. The minister replies that the government had always said it could not fully exclude incidental involvement of Afghan police in operations against the Taliban, that structural offensive use was not seen, and that the Chamber was informed of placement problems in 2012-2013.
The government could not and cannot fully exclude that incidentally Afghan civilian police could have been involved in military operations in Kunduz against the Taliban.
De regering kon en kan echter niet volledig uitsluiten dat incidenteel Afghaanse civiele agenten betrokken konden worden bij militaire operaties in Kunduz tegen de Taliban.
Antwoord op vragen van het lid Karabulut over openheid over gezondheidsrisico’s afvalverbranding op missies

MP Karabulut asks the Defence Minister why a 2008 risk assessment on waste burning (burn pits) at Tarin Kowt, which flagged health risks, was not disclosed in earlier answers, and why earlier health concerns were downplayed. The Minister answers that the 2008 report contained no new information, that air quality measurements showed no exceedance of health norms, and that the Chamber was informed in 2010-2011 and the relevant reports were made public.
Leading for me is that all relevant information is shared with the Chambers.
Leidend voor mij is dat alle relevante informatie wordt gedeeld met de Kamers.
Antwoord op vragen van het lid Bruins en Voordewind over het bericht ‘F-35 mag straks laagvliegen over oostelijk Fryslân’

MPs Bruins and Voordewind asked whether the government will reopen the Linkroute-10A low-flying route over eastern Friesland for F-35s, whether Friesland was involved, whether a nature permit is needed and whether alternatives were studied. The State Secretary for Defence answered that there is currently no reason to reopen the route, that a permit and ecological analysis are still being prepared, that alternatives abroad are being examined, and promised a decision by 1 June 2020.
At the consultation on 18 February I promised the House to provide clarity on the future of Linkroute-10A by 1 June 2020.
Tijdens het VAO op 18 februari heb ik uw Kamer toegezegd om voor 1 juni 2020 duidelijkheid te bieden over de toekomst van de Linkroute-10A.
Antwoord op vragen van de leden Groothuizen en Diertens over het bericht ‘Vreemdelingenadvocaten: ‘Curaçao zet Venezolanen collectief uit’

MPs Groothuizen and Diertens asked about reports that Curaçao collectively expelled Venezuelans and about detention conditions in the immigration barracks on Curaçao, including whether the Kingdom should intervene. The government answered that Curaçao is responsible for detention conditions, that Netherlands supports improvements, and that Kingdom intervention is a last resort, while promising continued monitoring and not committing to an independent visit.
Intervention by the Kingdom under the Charter is a last resort.
Ingrijpen door het Koninkrijk op grond van het Statuut is een laatste redmiddel.
Antwoord op vragen van het lid Kerstens over het Veteranenontmoetingscentrum (VOC) de Ouwestomp in Den Bosch

An MP from the Labour party asked the Defence Minister about the municipality of Den Bosch's handling of the Ouwestomp veterans' meeting centre, including its plan to change the site's use and alternative housing. The Minister answered that the municipality wants to find a joint solution, that VOCs are private initiatives not financed by Defence, that there are no fixed criteria for such centres, and that the municipality has confirmed it will offer suitable support, with the location and form left to local authorities.
It is up to the municipal administration to weigh the various local interests.
Het is immers aan het gemeentebestuur om de afweging te maken tussen de diverse lokale belangen.
Antwoord op vragen van het lid Karabulut over burgerslachtoffers door Nederlands optreden in de strijd tegen Islamitische Staat

MP Karabulut asked the Prime Minister and the Ministers of Foreign Affairs and Defence about civilian casualties from the Dutch bombing at Hawija in June 2015, including when officials were informed, whether information was withheld from parliament, and compensation. The government answers that the Prime Minister and Foreign Minister were informed only in general terms about secondary explosions and possible civilian harm without figures, that an ICRC list was not shared with parliament, that the OM investigation documents cannot be made public, and that compensation options and a progress letter are still being studied.
It was standing policy that for operational reasons and domestic security no statements were made about specific cases.
Het was staand beleid dat om operationele redenen en omwille van de binnenlandse veiligheid geen uitspraken werden gedaan over specifieke gevallen.
Antwoord op vragen van het lid Karabulut over vermeende “jarenlange misleiding over de oorlog in Afghanistan”

An SP MP asked the ministers of Foreign Affairs and Defence whether leaked US interviews showing repeated deception about the Afghanistan war, corruption, Afghan forces' readiness and progress, and the Dutch communication on it, were a concern. The government acknowledged the complexity and corruption problems, said the interviewees' views are personal, and admitted transparency and communication need improvement, referring to the post-mission review (PMB) Kunduz.
The cabinet underlines the importance of transparency about what does and does not go well in military and other deployments abroad.
Het kabinet onderstreept het belang van transparantie over wat er wel en niet goed gaat bij militaire en andere inzet in het buitenland.
Antwoord op vragen van de leden Krol en Van Helvert over de kranslegging op het oorlogskerkhof te Margaten

MPs Krol and Van Helvert asked why wreaths of balsam fir from the United States may stay on war graves in Margraten only 72 hours, and whether this could be changed given the tradition's importance to families. The Minister answered that the short period reflects EU plant health rules and pest risks, that the permit was granted exceptionally, and that a new risk analysis would be needed for any future request, while offering talks on alternatives.
If desired, I am happy to discuss with the initiators how we can meet the wishes regarding American wreath-laying traditions in an alternative way.
Desgewenst ga ik graag in gesprek met de initiatiefnemers hoe we op alternatieve wijze aan de wensen rond Amerikaanse kransleggingstradities tegemoet kunnen komen.

Antwoord op vragen van het lid Karabulut over de Amerikaanse luchtaanval op de internationale luchthaven van de Iraakse hoofdstad Bagdad, waarbij de Iraanse generaal Qassem Soleimani om het leven is gekomen

An SP MP asked the Foreign and Defence Ministers about the political consequences of the US strike at Baghdad airport that killed Qassem Soleimani, whether the government condemns it and its legality under international law, and whether the Hormuz naval deployment should be reconsidered. The ministers said Soleimani's militia role justified US concern but called for restraint, supported E3 dispute-settlement steps on the JCPOA, could not assess the US self-defence claim, and kept the EMASOH deployment while promising to inform parliament before departure if developments warrant.
If further developments give cause for this, they will be included in the letter that reaches your House before the Dutch frigate departs.
Indien verdere ontwikkelingen daartoe aanleiding geven, zullen deze worden meegenomen in de brief die uw Kamer toekomt, voor vertrek van het Nederlandse fregat
Antwoord op vragen van de leden Van Helvert, Sjoerdsma en Van Ojik over de Zembla-uitzending ‘Doelwit Volkel’

Three MPs asked whether the Netherlands has a veto over US nuclear weapons at Volkel, whether the Dutch pilots must follow a US order, and whether the government will confirm the presence of nuclear weapons. The ministers answered that NATO decisions require unanimity and Dutch consent, but that numbers, locations and procedures cannot be disclosed for security and binding alliance reasons, and that efforts to increase transparency have gained no support.

On the numbers and locations of US nuclear weapons present in Europe, as well as the precise procedures for nuclear decision-making and execution of the nuclear task, no information can be provided, on the basis of alliance and legally binding agreements.

Over aantallen en locaties van in Europa aanwezige Amerikaanse kernwapens, alsmede de precieze procedures voor nucleaire besluitvorming en uitvoering van de kernwapentaak kunnen, op grond van bondgenootschappelijke en juridisch bindende afspraken, geen mededelingen worden gedaan.
Antwoord op vragen van het lid Karabulut over Nederlands vetorecht in geval van inzet kernwapens

An SP MP asks whether the Netherlands has a veto over US nuclear weapon use, the legal basis for Dutch personnel's role, the 1992 nuclear accident agreement and the B61 modernisation. The ministers answer that NATO decisions require unanimity so Dutch consent is always needed, but refuse details on locations, procedures and the agreement citing security and NATO confidentiality obligations.

Regarding the number and locations of US nuclear weapons present in Europe, as well as the precise procedures for nuclear decision-making and execution of the nuclear task, no information can be provided, based on allied and legally binding agreements.

Over aantallen en locaties van in Europa aanwezige Amerikaanse kernwapens, alsmede de precieze procedures voor nucleaire besluitvorming en uitvoering van de kernwapentaak kunnen, op grond van bondgenootschappelijke en juridisch bindende afspraken, geen mededelingen worden gedaan.
Antwoord op vragen van het lid Popken over een bijna-kamikazeactie met een helikopter

An MP from the PVV asked the Defence Minister and State Secretary about a reported near-collision of a military helicopter with a riding stable during an exercise, and whether Defence would apologise and respond to complaints. The State Secretary denied any near-accident, said the flights were within the permit, that the stable owner was contacted by phone, and that no apology was due, while promising to examine incidents.
Antwoord op vragen van de leden Smeulders, Diks en Van Ojik over de investeringen van Nederlandse pensioenfondsen in controversiële wapenhandel

MPs Smeulders, Diks and Van Ojik asked the government about a PAX report showing Dutch pension funds invest over 1 billion euros in arms companies supplying Saudi Arabia, the UAE and Egypt, and what the government can do about it. The minister answered that pension investment policy is for funds and supervisors (AFM, DNB), that arms export rules were tightened for Saudi Arabia and the UAE, and that compliance with the IMVB pension covenant is voluntary but monitored.
It is not my task to supervise the investment policy of pension funds. That is for the supervisors, the Authority for the Financial Markets (AFM) and De Nederlandsche Bank (DNB).
Het is niet mijn taak om toezicht te houden op het beleggingsbeleid van pensioenfondsen. Dat is aan de toezichthouders Autoriteit Financiële Markt (AFM) en De Nederlandsche Bank (DNB).
Antwoord op vragen van de leden Belhaj, Groothuizen en Voordewind over het bericht 'Vluchtelingenwerk bezorgd om uitzetting Afghaanse tolk'

MPs Belhaj, Groothuizen and Voordewind asked whether an Afghan former interpreter for the US army, refused asylum and facing deportation, is consistent with government statements on risk groups for interpreters in Afghanistan, and how such cases are weighed. The government declined to discuss individual cases, explained that interpreters who worked for international missions are now treated as a systematically persecuted group following a motion, and estimated about ten former local staff granted asylum.
Antwoord op vragen van het lid Karabulut over door CENTCOM erkende burgerslachtoffers in Irak en Syrië

An MP asked the Defence and Foreign Affairs ministers whether the 1,346 civilian deaths acknowledged by CENTCOM in Iraq and Syria are confirmed, whether they include the Dutch strikes at Hawija and Mosul, and how the figures were verified. The minister answered that CENTCOM counts 1,347 confirmed civilian deaths, that the Hawija deaths were never confirmed and are excluded, and that the Mosul deaths (four) are included as credible.
The most recent monthly report of December 2 estimates that at least 1,347 civilian casualties resulted from actions of the anti-ISIS coalition.
In het meest recente maandelijkse overzicht van december 2 wordt ingeschat dat er ten minste 1.347 burgerslachtoffers te betreuren zijn ten gevolge van acties van de anti-ISIS coalitie.

Antwoord op vragen van de leden Van Helvert, Amhaouch, Bosman, Kerstens, Bruins, Voordewind en Stoffer over de berichtgeving ‘Nieuwe onderzeeboten: Nederlandse marine-industrie dreigt alleen kruimels te krijgen’

MPs from several parties asked the Defence, Finance and Economic Affairs ministers about press reports that the Dutch naval shipbuilding industry risks getting only scraps from the new submarine order, and about risks to knowledge retention, intellectual property, competition and the Defence Industry Strategy. The government answered at length, largely restating its procurement approach: competitive selection under Article 346 TFEU, IP and maintenance guarantees to be negotiated in the next phase, and no decision yet on a single preferred bidder.
As I stated in the B-letter, I will implement the Bruins Slot et al. motion.
Zoals ik in de B-brief heb vermeld zal ik uitvoering geven aan de motie Bruins Slot c.s.
Antwoord op vragen van het lid Popken over jarenlange sabotage van auto’s van militairen

An MP from PVV asked the Defence minister about reported long-running sabotage of military personnel's cars (loosened wheel bolts), whether earlier incidents were made public, what damage and costs resulted, and whether soldiers were compensated. The minister said the Military Police is investigating on behalf of the Public Prosecution Service, gave limited details on incidents and no findings, and noted a nationwide alert was issued.
I cannot make statements about the content of this investigation; that is up to the Public Prosecution Service.
Over de inhoud van dit onderzoek kan ik geen uitspraken doen, dat is aan het OM.
Antwoord op vragen van de leden Smeulders, Diks en Buitenweg over het bericht ‘Geheime diensten morren over nieuwe toezichthouder’

GroenLinks MPs asked whether the intelligence services are unhappy with the Toetsingscommissie Inzet Bevoegdheden (TIB), which authorises their special powers, over alleged assertive, detailed review and disputes about its scope and appeal rights. The minister acknowledges some disagreement on the scope of the TIB's legality review, says it is not a marginal review, and defers any change such as an appeal option to the evaluation of the Wiv 2017 starting in 2020.
As confirmed during the parliamentary treatment of the Wiv 2017, the TIB's review is not a marginal review.
Zoals tijdens de parlementaire behandeling van de Wiv 2017 is bevestigd, is de toets van de TIB géén marginale toets.
Antwoord op vragen van de leden De Roon, Popken en Helder over piraterij in de Golf van Mexico

MPs De Roon, Popken and Helder asked the ministers of Foreign Affairs, Defence and Justice and Security about piracy in the Gulf of Mexico, including the reported rise in attacks, any signals of attacks on Dutch-flagged ships, monitoring and cooperation, and whether armed private guards could be allowed on Dutch ships. The government answered that it cannot confirm the attack figures, has received no signals of attacks on Dutch-flagged ships, relies on cooperation with the US and Mexico, and noted that armed guards may become possible under the new Wet ter Bescherming Koopvaardij in designated High Risk Areas, which the Gulf is not currently.
To date we have not yet received any signals that ships sailing under the Dutch flag were targeted by pirates in the Gulf of Mexico.
Tot op heden hebben wij nog geen signalen ontvangen dat schepen varende onder de Nederlandse vlag doelwit waren van piraten in de Golf van Mexico.
Antwoord op vragen van het lid Van Dam over het bericht 'Gevangenis Pointe Blanche: The Devil’s Rock van Sint Maarten'

An MP asked about reports on the Pointe Blanche prison in Sint Maarten, progress on improvement measures, the status of Council of Europe supervision after the Corallo judgment, and whether TBS (ter beschikking stelling) can be imposed and executed in the Caribbean parts of the Kingdom. The Minister reported slow progress on prison improvements, marine assistance in late October and November, periodic monitoring with Sint Maarten, that Council of Europe assessment is awaited in early 2020, and that TBS is executed by the countries themselves with no facilities in the Netherlands.
With Sint Maarten, progress on the agreed improvement measures is reviewed every 2 weeks.
Met Sint Maarten wordt elke 2 weken gekeken naar de voortgang van de afgesproken verbetermaatregelen.
Antwoord op vragen van het lid Karabulut over een luchtaanval op Mosul, Irak, waarbij vier burgers werden gedood

MPs Karabulut asked about a 2015 Mosul airstrike, attributed to the Netherlands, that killed four civilians, including why it took so long to acknowledge responsibility, why the coalition's investigations and CENTCOM reports are not shared, and whether compensation is available. The minister answered that Dutch involvement was reported to CENTCOM, that the targeting was judged lawful at the time, that CENTCOM reports are US-classified, that secrecy was needed for security reasons until recently, and that a voluntary compensation proposal will be sent to parliament.
The Netherlands therefore cannot unilaterally make these reports public.
Nederland kan deze rapporten dan ook niet eenzijdig openbaar maken.
Antwoord op vragen van het lid Van Dam over het bericht ‘Harddrugs gevonden bij een militair op marineschip Curaçao’

Members of parliament asked whether cocaine was found on a navy ship in Curaçao, about the zero-tolerance drug policy, drug seizures from Curaçao, and the working of drug scanners at Curaçao's airport and port. The government confirmed about 11 kg of suspected cocaine found with a soldier, explained its zero-tolerance policy and seizure figures, and said border controls on Curaçao are an autonomous matter, with Schiphol applying 100% Customs checks on arrivals.
Two incidents are still under criminal investigation and no further information can be given on them at this time.
Twee incidenten worden nog strafrechtelijk onderzocht en daarover kan op dit moment geen nadere informatie worden gegeven.
Antwoord op vragen van de leden Van Ojik en Diks over het bericht dat de minister van Defensie niet aanwezig was bij de bijeenkomst van NAVO-ministers van Buitenlandse Zaken op 20 november 2019

MPs Van Ojik and Diks asked why the Defence Minister did not attend the NATO foreign ministers' meeting on 20 November 2019, as reported by Trouw. The government answered that the Defence Minister stayed in The Hague to prepare for a possible parliamentary debate on transparency about civilian casualties, and that Netherlands' permanent NATO representative attended instead.

Yes, the Minister of Defence took into account a possible wish of your House to hold a debate in the short term on transparency about civilian casualties, and therefore decided not to travel to Brussels.

Ja, de Minister van Defensie hield rekening met een mogelijke wens van uw Kamer om op korte termijn een debat te voeren over de transparantie over burgerslachtoffers en heeft daarom besloten om niet naar Brussel af te reizen.
Antwoord op vragen van het lid Diks over de aanwezigheid van informatie op ministeries over de burgerdoden bij het Nederlandse bombardement op Hawija

MP Diks asked ministers whether ministries had been informed about the outcome of the CENTCOM investigation into civilian deaths at Hawija and whether the Defence Minister misinformed parliament in 2015. The government answers that ministries received only general, non-numerical information in 2015 meetings, the initial CENTCOM report was not shared with other departments, and the 2015 statements to parliament were found to be incorrect.
The initial CENTCOM report as such was never provided to other departments, in line with standing practice.
Het initiële CENTCOM-rapport als zodanig is nooit verstrekt aan andere departementen, conform staande praktijk.
Antwoord op vragen van het lid Karabulut over de besluitvorming over geheimhouding burgerslachtoffers in Irak in 2015

The MPs asked how and when ministers were informed of civilian casualties in the 2015 Dutch air operation at Hawija, Iraq, whether the matter was discussed in ministerial sub-councils, and whether the Prime Minister was involved in keeping it secret. The Defence Minister answered that ministers were briefed in June 2015 on the basis of the After Action Report, that civilian casualties remain unconfirmed, that no decision to keep the facts secret was ever taken, and that the matter was not specifically discussed in the relevant sub-councils.
No, such a decision has never been taken.
Nee, van een dergelijke beslissing is nooit sprake geweest.
Antwoord op vragen van het lid Karabulut over een passage uit het boek Missie F-16 over mogelijke burgerslachtoffers in Irak

An SP MP asks the defence and foreign ministers about a reported Dutch F-16 strike in Iraq at Christmas 2014 that may have hit civilians, and why it was never reported to parliament, and asks whether other unreported strikes exist. The minister answers that analysts doubted civilian harm at the time, it was quickly ruled out, CENTCOM investigated and found none, and that all reported Dutch cases with possible civilian harm have been disclosed to parliament.
The Ministry of Defence therefore saw no reason to launch an investigation into this case.
Het Ministerie van Defensie zag daarom geen aanleiding om een onderzoek in te stellen naar dit geval.
Antwoord op vragen van het lid Karabulut over een Nederlandse luchtaanval in Irak waarbij tientallen burgerslachtoffers zouden zijn gevallen

An MP from the SP asked the ministers of Defence and Foreign Affairs about a Dutch airstrike in Hawija, Iraq in June 2015 that reportedly killed around seventy civilians, asking whether the Chamber was misinformed, whether targeting was careful, whether compensation was paid, whether the OM investigated, and whether other strikes were withheld. The Defence minister answered that the Chamber was informed in 2018 without exact details due to an ongoing operation, that the strike caused unintended collateral damage, that the targeting process was careful, that no victims claimed Dutch compensation, and that the OM found no reason for prosecution, promising a further letter on transparency.
In my letter of 4 November 2019 (reference BS2019018779) on the feasibility of greater transparency about possible civilian casualties from air strikes, I will elaborate on the reasons
In mijn brief van 4 november 2019 (referentie BS2019018779) over de haalbaarheid van meer transparantie over mogelijke burgerslachtoffers bij luchtaanvallen, ga ik nader in op de redenen
Antwoord op vragen van de leden Van den Bosch en Laan-Geselschap inzake “het krijgen van een assistentiehond”

MPs Van den Bosch and Laan-Geselschap asked why the PTSD assistance-dog study for veterans has not yet concluded and why waiting lists and limited choice of trainers persist. The minister replies that the first study was finished and presented in June 2018, that a follow-up longitudinal study with Utrecht University is expected to report in September 2021, and that the results will guide future policy on dog deployment, training and funding.
The research result is expected to be ready in September 2021. Defence is of course following this closely.
Het onderzoeksresultaat zal naar verwachting in september 2021 gereed zijn. Defensie volgt dit uiteraard aandachtig.
Antwoord op vragen van de leden Belhaj, Van Weyenberg en Paternotte over het bericht ‘Een ongeluk waar je niets van leert’

Three D66 MPs asked the Defence and Infrastructure ministers about a 2018 helicopter training accident involving the Coast Guard's SAR contractor, the unreported incident, and unclear inspection and safety responsibilities across ILT, Inspectie SZW and contractors. The government answered that the accident was reported by the worker, that an inspection into the employer's failure to report will be started, and that responsibilities are divided among several inspectorates, while rejecting claims of unacceptable shortcomings.
ISZW will launch an investigation into this.
Er wordt door ISZW een onderzoek hiernaar ingesteld.
Antwoord op vragen van het lid Karabulut over de aanwezigheid van een Nederlandse militaire functionaris bij een militaire conferentie in Saoedi-Arabië

MP Karabulut asked the Defence Minister whether a Dutch military official attended a Saudi-hosted military conference on 21 October 2019 about military aid to Saudi Arabia, why the Netherlands accepted, and what was requested and agreed. The minister answered that no Dutch military official attended, only an embassy secretary as observer, that no Dutch commitments were made, and that the conference produced no concrete results beyond Saudi information-sharing.
During the international conference in Saudi Arabia on 21 October, no Dutch military official was present.
Tijdens de internationale conferentie in Saoedi-Arabië van 21 oktober jl. was geen Nederlandse militaire functionaris aanwezig.
Antwoord op vragen van het lid Belhaj over het bericht 'De Nederlandse ‘precisiebom’ op een wapendepot van IS'

An MP from D66 asked the Defence and Foreign Affairs ministers about reports of a Dutch precision bomb on an IS arms depot near Hawija in June 2015, including the targeting checks, civilian casualties, transparency and compensation. The minister answered that Dutch targeting checks were applied, that the strike caused unintended secondary explosions and roughly 70 casualties, that Dutch involvement is now acknowledged, and that compensation falls to Iraq and no individual claims were made to Defence.
This Hawija case was one of the cases mentioned there.
Dit geval in Hawija betrof een van de daar vermelde gevallen.
Antwoord  op vragen van de leden Wilders, Fritsma en Emiel van Dijk over aan Defensie gerelateerde kosten van Nederlanders met een migratieachtergrond

PVV MPs asked the Defence Ministry for the costs attributable to people with a non-Western migration background, including Marechaussee enforcement of removals, chaplaincy and halal catering, and the benefits those groups bring. The government answered that Defence has no insight into costs by migration background, gave Marechaussee Vreemdelingenwet costs of EUR 184.8 million in 2018 without any breakdown by origin, and described the chaplaincy and catering arrangements without attributing costs to specific groups.
Defence has no insight into the costs arising from the presence of citizens with a (non-Western/Western) migration background in the Netherlands.
Defensie heeft geen inzicht in de kosten die voortvloeien uit de aanwezigheid van burgers met een (niet-westerse/westerse) migratieachtergrond in Nederland.
Antwoord op vragen van het lid Diks over het bericht dat een onderzoek over burnpits jarenlang op de plank heeft gelegen

An MP asked the Defence Minister why a 2012 TNO report on burn pit monitoring methods was not sent to Parliament in full, why Defence downplayed its health relevance, and when a validation of the CEAG literature review would be completed. The minister admitted it would have been better to publish the report, released it, and said validation is being re-tendered after RIVM declined, with the scope limited to the literature review rather than combination toxicity.
In hindsight, it would probably have been better to make the report public.
Achteraf gezien was het waarschijnlijk beter geweest het rapport openbaar te maken.
Antwoord op vragen van het lid Karabulut over hulp aan veteranen die lijden aan PTSS

MP Karabulut (SP) asked the Defence Minister what concrete steps will improve veterans' PTSS care, whether the Thuisbasis Veteranen in Eelde's experiences warrant new measures, and how the duty of care applies to veterans who avoid care or are homeless. The minister replied that the existing care system is sound with ongoing improvements, that no new measures are needed, that Defence has no oversight of care-avoiders, and that the Thuisbasis is a civilian institution outside Defence's system.
Neither Defence nor anyone else has insight into the numbers of veterans who avoid care or wander about.
Defensie noch anderen hebben zicht op de aantallen veteranen die zorg mijden dan wel rondzwerven.
Antwoord op vragen van het lid Popken over het Europees Defensiefonds

An MP asks the Defence Minister why the Chamber learned from the media that TNO lobbied for European defence funds, whether the Chamber will be given withheld information, and whether non-EU countries can participate in the European Defence Fund, plus challenges the fund's design. The minister answers that the Chamber was regularly informed via BNC-fiches and debates, will review sharing withheld information under Article 68 of the Constitution, and explains that the fund is open to consortia in the EU and EEA associated states subject to safeguards, while endorsing the Commission's analysis.
You will be informed about this.
Antwoord op vragen van het lid Öztürk over het optreden van KMar- en douanemedewerkers op Schiphol, Eindhoven Airport en Rotterdam The Hague Airport

An MP asks ministers about alleged ethnic profiling and discriminatory treatment by Customs and the Royal Netherlands Marechaussee at Schiphol and Eindhoven airports, including an Ombudsman finding on Customs cash checks. The government denies systematic profiling, acknowledges shortcomings in information provision and one inappropriate remark, cites ongoing complaint procedures, and declines a separate investigation while awaiting the Ombudsman's own inquiry.
Yes, Customs acknowledges that at the time of the complaint the provision of information at Eindhoven Airport was insufficient
Ja, de Douane erkent dat ten tijde van de klacht de informatieverstrekking op Eindhoven Airport onvoldoende was
Antwoord op vragen van het lid Popken over het bericht dat een konvooi met Nederlands legermaterieel is aangevallen in Mali.

An MP asked the Defence Minister about an attack on a convoy carrying Dutch military equipment in Mali, the deteriorating security situation, duty of care for personnel, and whether the MINUSMA mission should be halted. The minister expressed regret for Malian deaths, defended MINUSMA's relevance and mandate adjustment, and stated the redeployment is complete with remaining equipment returning in Q2 2020.
I deeply regret that six Malians (four soldiers and two drivers) died in the attack on the convoy carrying Dutch equipment on 21 August 2019.
Ik betreur ten zeerste dat zes Malinezen (vier militairen en twee chauffeurs) zijn omgekomen bij de aanslag op het konvooi met Nederlands materieel op 21 augustus 2019.
Antwoord op vragen van de leden Van Haga en Bosman over het kabinetsbeleid ten aanzien van de defensie-industrie

MPs Van Haga and Bosman ask the government to reconcile its support for the domestic defence industry with its strict arms-export policy and with the FMO exclusion list that bars firms earning 10% or more from weapons from trade-promotion and financing instruments such as DTIF. The ministers confirm the policy tension, state that generic trade instruments are now open to defence firms, and say the government will review remaining aspects of defence trade support by Prinsjesdag 2019 while denying any intent to penalise the sector.
At present, however, the cabinet is considering whether trade support for the defence sector can be adjusted on this point in light of the DIS.
Op dit moment beziet het kabinet echter of de handelsinzet voor de defensiesector op dit punt in het licht van de DIS kan worden aangepast
Antwoord op vragen van de leden Van Haga en Bosman over de impact van het eenzijdig aangescherpte wapenexportbeleid voor de concurrentiepositie van de Nederlandse defensie-industrie

MPs Van Haga and Bosman asked about the impact of the Dutch tightened arms export policy toward the UAE, Egypt and Saudi Arabia on the competitiveness of the Dutch defence industry, including comparisons with German, French, Spanish and Czech practice, the Dutch military presence in the UAE, and whether defence firms can join trade missions. The government answered that the Netherlands is not acting alone since Germany and Finland also restricted exports, that the policy is justified by international obligations and humanitarian law, and that it regrets the negative effects on Dutch defence firms while pursuing harmonisation within the EU and opening trade missions to defence firms.
Arms export control is a national competence. EU member states are themselves responsible for assessing arms export applications against the eight criteria of the EU Common Position on arms exports.

Wapenexportcontrole is een nationale bevoegdheid. EU-lidstaten zijn zelf verantwoordelijk voor de toetsing van wapenexportaanvragen aan de acht criteria van het EU Gemeenschappelijk Standpunt inzake wapenexport.
Antwoord op vragen van het lid Bosman over discriminatie van de defensie-industrie door het kabinet tegen de achtergrond van de Defensie Industrie Strategie

MP Bosman asks the government why the defence industry was excluded from trade missions and Dutch trade instruments, whether this fits the Defence Industry Strategy, and why earlier written questions remained unanswered. The government replies that generic trade instruments such as trade missions and Partners In Business are now open to defence firms with over 10% of activity in weapons or ammunition, while the Dutch Trade and Investment Fund remains under review and the delay was due to interdepartmental coordination.
The cabinet has instructed the implementers of its generic trade promotion instruments to make this adjustment.
Het kabinet heeft de uitvoerders van zijn generieke handelsbevorderende instrumenten opgedragen om deze aanpassing door te voeren.
Antwoord op vragen van het lid Belhaj over het bericht ‘Geef burger ook veteranenstatus’

An MP asked whether civilian personnel (diplomats, police, aid workers) deployed alongside soldiers in mission areas should receive veteran status and access to the same care. The government answered that civilians receive recognition via the Herinneringsmedaille and existing care arrangements, but that veteran status under the Veteranenwet is tied to the special legal position of military personnel and is therefore not appropriate for civilians.
On the basis of the Veterans Act and the provisions based on it, granting veteran status to diplomats, police officers and aid workers is therefore not appropriate.
Op basis van de Veteranenwet en de daarop berustende bepalingen is het toekennen van de veteranenstatus aan diplomaten, politieagenten en hulpverleners derhalve niet opportuun.
Antwoord op vragen van het lid Belhaj over het bericht ‘’Russen’ intimideren vrouwen Nederlandse F16-vliegers’

An MP asked the Defence Minister whether reports that Russia intimidates the wives of Dutch F-16 pilots are accurate, how often this happens, and what protection Defence offers military personnel and families. The minister acknowledged the hybrid threat and described briefings, reporting procedures and a VPN service, but gave no incident figures and said attribution is not always possible.
Is there anything to say, if necessary confidentially, about how often this has happened in recent years and whether these intimidation practices have increased?
Is er iets te zeggen, desnoods vertrouwelijk, over hoe vaak dit de afgelopen jaren is gebeurd en in welke mate sprake is van een toename van deze intimidatiepraktijken?
Antwoord op vragen van het lid Bosman over de inzet van Defensie in het ruimtevaartdomein

An MP asked the Defence Minister about the Netherlands' role in the space domain, including NATO's space policy, investments, cooperation with Norway, the Brik-II military satellite and the Defence Space Security Centre. The minister answered at length on NATO's space policy, investment levels and cooperation, but gave largely descriptive, policy-restating answers without new commitments or oversight-related information.
Defence recognises the military importance of space and space capabilities.
Defensie onderkent het militair belang van de ruimte en ruimtecapaciteiten.
Antwoord op vragen van de leden Popken en Fritsma over het bericht dat bij een Duits-Nederlandse grenscontrole 27 overtredingen van de Vreemdelingenwet zijn geconstateerd

Two PVV MPs asked the ministers about reports of 27 Immigration Act violations found at a joint German-Dutch border check, including nationalities, criminal records, Islamic background, detentions and deportations, and whether borders should be closed to asylum seekers and Islamic-country migrants. The government answered that 10 Dutch-side cases involved persons without residence permits (nationalities listed, no criminal records found, religion not registered), rejected categorical border closure as unrealistic, and noted the Marechaussee already performs border surveillance.
Based on information and registers available to the Marechaussee, no criminal records were found for the 10 persons named.
Op basis van bij de KMar beschikbare informatie en registers zijn bij de 10 genoemde personen geen criminele antecedenten gebleken.
Antwoord op vragen van het lid Kerstens over het bericht “Dutchbat veteraan: excuses zouden ons enorm goed doen”

An MP asked the Defence Minister about a news report on Dutchbat-III veterans who want apologies, the timeline for the research and commission results, whether concrete steps will follow, and how veterans will be kept informed. The minister answered that a research project led by ARQ Nationaal Psychotrauma Centrum runs until mid-2020 under an independent commission, that follow-up steps depend on its findings, and that contact with the Dutchbat-III association and a low-threshold contact point will keep veterans informed.
The concrete follow-up steps are explicitly linked to the outcomes of the research.
De concrete vervolgstappen zijn nadrukkelijk verbonden aan de uitkomsten van het onderzoek
Antwoord op vragen van de leden Belhaj en Sjoerdsma over het bericht ‘Commando’s: ’de Baas’ heeft veel dodelijke aanslagen voorkomen’

MPs Belhaj and Sjoerdsma asked the Defence Minister about a report that a human source ('Windhond32') working for the MIVD prevented many deadly attacks, including claims about his debts, PTSD treatment, and a request for a meeting, and about a letter from Commando troops. The Minister declined to confirm or comment on the MIVD's activities and sources, citing the need for care with human sources, and said an unsigned letter could not be answered specifically.
I cannot make any public statements about the activities of the MIVD and the possible deployment of human sources.
Over de activiteiten van de MIVD en de eventuele inzet van menselijke bronnen kan ik in het openbaar geen mededelingen doen.
